title: CTSA Human-Return Readout: A Session-Boundary Measurement Architecture for Retained Human Capability After AI (Epistemic Note v9.1 FINAL)

equations.label: CTSA-01
equations.text: Δ^ret_H = R_Q(S^post_H) − R_Q(S^pre_H), where R_Q is a declared reader/question and S^pre_H, S^post_H are bounded task-relative descriptions of the human before AI exposure and after an unaided return interval.
equations.meaning: Architectural notation (not a validated psychological metric) for the task-relevant retained difference recoverable by a declared reader.

equations.label: CTSA-02
equations.section: 5.2 Meaning, persistence, and truth remain non-identical
equations.meaning: Restates the Epistemic Fusion/Tunnel non-collapse: retained CTSA items are knowledge-like candidates, not automatically validated knowledge.

equations.label: CTSA-03
equations.text: C → T → Workflow → S → A → C′.
equations.meaning: A useful but non-mandatory relation among CTSA classes and workflow, illustrating role separation, not a universal causal law.

equations.label: CTSA-04
equations.text: R_H = ⟨G_CTSA, L, M, P, W, Δ_dir⟩.
equations.meaning: Bookkeeping tuple (not a calibrated universal score) combining Gain profile, Loss profile, Metacognitive regulation, Provenance, Warrant, and epistemic Direction.

equations.label: CTSA-05
equations.text: Frozen Human baseline → K_like → Difference/Resistance → H↔AI → Retention gate → CTSA Return Profile → Unaided Return Test → Gain/Loss → Regulation → Provenance/Warrant → Epistemic direction.
equations.meaning: The full programme sequence placing CTSA at the boundary where conversational residue is claimed to become human capability.

equations.label: NCL-10
equations.text: AI fluency ≠ human baseline; explanation ≠ verification; output count ≠ epistemic diversity; exposure ≠ retention ≠ improvement; trust in AI ≠ calibrated confidence in self; augmentation ≠ synergy ≠ Human Return; retained gain ≠ net expansion; provenance ≠ warrant; persistence ≠ truth.
equations.meaning: Nine non-collapse laws carried over and preserved from the programme's earlier work.

equations.label: H1
equations.text: Incremental Readout Hypothesis [Open]: a CTSA Return Profile will explain reproducible variance in delayed unaided human capability beyond ordinary post-test performance, recall, confidence, and established concept/skill measures.
equations.meaning: Open hypothesis on incremental predictive validity of CTSA.

equations.label: H2
equations.text: Partial Dissociation Hypothesis [Open]: Conceptual, Tool-Selection, Skill-Execution, and Alternative-Generation returns will show partially dissociable profiles under matched interaction conditions rather than one interchangeable gain.
equations.meaning: Open hypothesis that the four CTSA classes are separable, not fungible.

equations.label: H3
equations.text: Return-vs-Exposure Prediction [Externally constrained]: items visible only while AI support is present will predict assisted performance more strongly than delayed unaided capability.
equations.meaning: Hypothesis externally supported in general form by Bastani et al., though not specifically for CTSA classes.

equations.label: H4
equations.text: Gain/Loss Asymmetry Hypothesis [Open]: positive CTSA gain can coexist with negative loss in previously accessible routes/checking habits; gross gain will overestimate net human expansion.

equations.label: H5
equations.text: Recombination Hypothesis [Open]: CTSA gains will sometimes interact compositionally (new Concept improves Tool selection; Tool+Skill make an Alternative accessible; new Alternative triggers conceptual restructuring).
equations.meaning: Open hypothesis on compositional interaction among CTSA classes.

equations.label: H6
equations.text: Regulation/Direction Hypothesis [Open]: equal gross CTSA gains will yield different later corrigibility depending on metacognitive calibration, effective resistance, provenance visibility, and semantic-basin dynamics.
equations.meaning: Open hypothesis on the role of regulation/direction in interpreting gains.
